chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Yahya al-Lahham from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who married a slave woman alongside a free woman, he said:

If the free woman wishes to remain with the slave woman, she may remain; and if she wishes, she may go to her family. I said to him: If she does not consent to this and goes to her family, does he have authority over her if she does not consent to staying? He said: He has no authority over her if she does not consent when she knows. I said: Then her going to her family is her divorce. He said: Yes, when she leaves his house, she observes a waiting period of three months or three menstrual periods, then she may marry if she wishes.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a free woman when her master marries a slave woman and she chooses to leave?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the legal autonomy of a free woman married to a master who also holds a slave woman, emphasizing that her voluntary departure to her family constitutes a revocable divorce (talaq) rather than mere separation. This ruling highlights the distinct status of the *hurrah* compared to the *ama*, granting the free woman the right to exit the marriage without the husband's consent, thereby triggering a three-month or three-menses waiting period (*iddah*) before she may remarry.
